gen-dafont-college-fs-hind: Every curve in College is as fat as its straight stems, with big open counters. Hind follows with lowercase nearly the height of its capitals and a steady, string-like stroke, so paragraphs run along smoothly in sans-serif without a snag.
gen-dafont-college-fs-paquito:
Paquito reads confident and friendly, its lowercase nearly touching cap height.

College hits hardest with its uniform, chunky strokes and tall open counters, while the classic serif body does its best work quietly, holding steady lines of text.
gen-dafont-college-fs-pilcrow-rounded:
Warm and dense, Pilcrow Rounded packs its letters tight.

College shouts with thick, stem-heavy curves and tall counters above it, and the plain sans body below keeps its own big, open curves, so the headline's punch lands and the text still feels friendly.
gen-dafont-college-fs-ranade: College opens with bold letters of uniform thickness, no thick-thin shifts anywhere in its curves and stems. Ranade's soft, pencil-like stroke change is the pairing's best quality.
gen-dafont-college-fs-rowan:
Rowan is literary and friendly, with generous curves.

College's tall lowercase makes a strong contrast with its moderate height, so a text serif body this size looks best a notch or two below the heading.
gen-dafont-college-gf-cascadia-code:
Modern and wiry, Cascadia Code spaces its letters far apart.

College is dynamic and authoritative with thick, even curves, and the monoline sans-serif skeleton below it stays smooth around every bend, which is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-college-gf-headland-one:
Headland One reads dignified and traditional, its letters spaced well apart.

Over a long passage its tall rounded o and gentle stroke contrast feel unhurried and formal, a quiet counterweight to College's uniform, outline-thick heading.
gen-dafont-college-sora:
Punchy, thick and tall-lowercase College faces off against Sora, whose precise geometry keeps curves flat in pressure.

Next to each other, a high lowercase and a moderate one feel crisp and deliberate.
gen-dafont-commodore-64-fs-rowan:
Commodore 64 looks snug and shuttered, with fixed-width, code-style letters.

Rowan's open curves and thick-thin strokes, in a classic serif, make a long passage feel friendly and literary, almost a relief after the heading's tight lowercase.
gen-dafont-conthrax-fs-karma:
Karma is a trustworthy serif with a barely taller cap height.

Over a long passage its calm, gradually tapering strokes never snag the eye, a soft landing after Conthrax's geometric, single-thread heading.
